title: Laras and the Silent Gong
blurb: The big gong has vanished four days before the school show. Laras and Bayu follow the clues.

chapters.title: The Gong Is Gone
chapters.text:
On Monday morning, Laras ran to the music room at her school in Yogyakarta. The gamelan group was going to practise for the school show on Friday. But when she opened the door, she stopped. The big bronze gong was gone! There was only an empty wooden stand.

Her friend Bayu rushed in behind her. "Did someone take it?" he gasped.

"It is too heavy for one person," said Laras. She frowned. "And the door was locked all weekend."

Their teacher, Bu Sari, looked worried. "The show is in four days," she said. "We need that gong."

Laras took a small notebook from her bag. "Then we will find it," she said. "I am going to be a detective."

chapters.title: Muddy Clues
chapters.text:
Laras and Bayu searched the room. Bayu looked under the drums. Laras studied the floor. Near the empty stand, she found a line of dry mud with wide, round marks in it.

"These are not footprints," she said. "They look like wheel marks."

They followed the marks into the corridor. The marks stopped at the back door, which was a little open. Bayu pushed it. Outside, the marks crossed the yard towards the old workshop where the caretaker kept his tools.

"Wheels," said Bayu. "Maybe someone used a trolley."

Laras wrote in her notebook: Clue one, wheel marks from the music room to the workshop. Then she noticed something else. On the door handle there was a tiny white petal.

chapters.title: The Smell of Jasmine
chapters.text:
The workshop door was shut, but the children could smell something sweet. "Jasmine," said Laras. She held up the petal. "The same smell."

Just then, Pak Min the caretaker walked across the yard. He always wore a straw hat with a fresh jasmine flower tucked in the band. When he saw the children, he stopped. He looked very nervous.

"Good morning," he said quickly. "I am busy today. Please do not come near the workshop."

Bayu whispered, "He is hiding something."

Laras shook her head slowly. "A clue is not proof," she said. "Many people wear jasmine in Yogyakarta. Let us watch and wait."

chapters.title: A Hum in the Workshop
chapters.text:
At lunchtime, Laras and Bayu crept towards the workshop again. They did not go inside. They stood by the window, which was a little open.

They heard a soft hum, and a tap, tap, tap. Someone was singing a gamelan tune while working.

Bayu stood on a box and peeped through the gap. His eyes grew wide. "Laras," he whispered. "I can see the gong! It is standing on a table, and Pak Min is rubbing it with a cloth."

Laras climbed up beside him. The gong was shining like gold in the sun. Next to it stood the music stand with new wood where there used to be a crack.

"Why would Pak Min hide it?" asked Bayu.

chapters.title: The Surprise
chapters.text:
Laras decided not to guess any more. She knocked on the workshop door. Pak Min opened it, and his face went red.

"Oh dear," he said. "You found my secret. I am so sorry. I should have left a note."

He explained everything. Last week he saw a crack in the wooden stand. He was afraid that the heavy gong would fall during the show. So on Saturday he rolled the gong on a trolley to the workshop, mended the stand, and polished the bronze. "I wanted to give Bu Sari a surprise," he said.

That afternoon, Pak Min and the children pushed the gong back to the music room. Bu Sari clapped her hands. On Friday the gamelan played beautifully. Laras wrote one last line in her notebook: Case closed. Ask first, guess later.
